About us

YourNest Venture Capital is a sharply focused 'Pre-Series A' fund house that was established in 2011 to nurture global market leaders from India. It invests in technology-led, enterprise-driven (B2B) and DeepTech (IoT, SaaS) startups. We are seeing India swiftly shift from an IT service outsourcing-hub to an IP/Patent driven 'Product Nation' with compelling investment opportunities. Our first fund of US$ 14 mn, started in 2012, invested in 16 companies and closed at a DPI of 3.3x. We launched our second fund of US$ 30 in 2017 mn and invested in 19 Indian startups with a focus on DeepTech. As of March 2021, CRISIL ranked it 7th among 48 AIFs launched in FY17. While several exits have been taking place from both funds, some of the Fund II portfolio companies – including Miko, Dozee and Exponent Energy – have already shown early promise of being Dragons i.e. companies that can potentially return the entire fund corpus in a single exit. YourNest Innovative Products VC Fund III – was launched in 2021 and is likely to close at US$ 100 mn, after exercising the greenshoe option. As of June 2026, we have launched a Rs 400 crore continuation fund, YourNest Continuum Fund I, anchored by HDFC AMC Select FoF I SEBI registration numbers for our four funds: Fund I: IN/AIF1/25-26/1874 Fund II: IN/AIF1/16-17/0267 Fund III: IN/AIF2/20-21/0863 Continuum Fund I: IN/AIF2/25-26/1919

We are delighted to welcome Roneet Parikh, who joins YourNest as part of the Investment Growth team. In this role, he will work with early-stage companies in our portfolio, helping founders navigate the challenges of building and scaling their businesses. 

Roneet’s experience spans startup research, Founder’s Office roles at AI and tech startups, and building his own local delivery startup during the pandemic. Across these assignments, he developed a keen interest in technology-led businesses, especially AI and DeepTech. During his undergraduate degree he studied Computer Science at Narsee Monjee Institute of Management Studies, and Innovation & Entrepreneurship at the University of Warwick for his Master's. Computer Science taught him to break down complex problems, while entrepreneurship gave him the business perspective to think about customers, markets and business models. 

What sets Roneet apart is his habit of taking ownership of problems rather than waiting to be told how to solve them. He gets close to the problem, speaks to the people involved and works out what would actually help. He prefers practical solutions that can be tested and improved over chasing perfection upfront. 

The YourNest team grows stronger with people who bring this kind of ownership and curiosity and we’re excited to see the impact he’ll make. 

Welcome aboard, Roneet!

Almost everyone who works for a living experiences what they call ‘Mondayitis’ at some point or the other… unless you’re either building something that’ll change the way we live, work and even play; or enabling the builders who are leveraging technology in ways unimagined. 

And that’s what we saw when a bunch of our Delhi NCR startup founders, the YourNest Venture Capital, Portfolio Managers and Functional Heads came over to Gurgaon yesterday evening. In a visible display of unflagging energy synonymous with entrepreneurs, conversations continued over cocktails (and nimbu-paani!). There was a sense of camaraderie – not just between old-timers but also folks who met for the first time yesterday. They came from as far as Jodhpur and Indore too, and established bonds that are sure to go further over time and geography. 

I had the unique experience of dining on Kung-pao Chicken with Jeera Rice – not quite fusion, but confusion! And we also had an uninvited guest that’s survived many millennia and has inspired the name of a protesting political party much in the news these days… but the creature was quickly expelled, much to the chagrin of the five-star hotel whose hygiene levels will certainly need an upgrade.

Most of the attendees are tagged in the photos here, but we also had many others who made the evening truly memorable! Thank you for being there.

We are delighted to welcome Shivanshu Mishra, who joins YourNest as Senior Analyst in the Investment Management team. In this role, he will focus on deal execution, portfolio and compliance tracking, and shareholder rights management, ensuring every portfolio company is on track, both operationally and strategically.

Shivanshu brings experience across DefenceTech, HealthTech, CleanTech, FinTech, AgriTech and enterprise SaaS, spanning early-stage venture and institutional investing. He holds an MBA in Finance & Strategy from IIM Raipur, and has a B.Tech in Electronics from IET DAVV, Indore. He has also cleared CFA Level 1. His engineering background taught him to break problems into first principles, while finance taught him to price uncertainty. He rarely takes a number or a narrative at face value.

What sets Shivanshu apart is a habit of flagging problems before they become crises and not waiting until the deadline. He is happiest building structure where none exists, taking an ambiguous mandate and creating a framework that works under pressure. The YourNest team grows stronger with people who bring this kind of rigour and discipline, and we’re excited to see the impact he’ll make.

Welcome aboard, Shivanshu!

We are delighted to welcome Saumya Dubey, who joins YourNest as Senior Analyst, MD's Office. Working closely with our Managing Director, Sunil Goyal, she will drive execution across projects, programme management, research briefs, and stakeholder support for the board, advisors and shareholders.

Saumya brings experience across venture capital in ClimateTech and HealthTech, journalism, culture writing, and the non-profit space. She holds a BA Honours in Psychology from Lady Shri Ram College and an MA in Psychology from Indraprastha College for Women. She also holds an NISM-Series-XIX-D AIF Managers certification. Her academic grounding in psychology shapes how she frames diligence questions, always looking at incentives, behaviour and the story behind the numbers. 

Saumya's disciplined approach sets her apart: she reads every piece of work that crosses her desk once for the overall argument, and then again line by line for numbers and assumptions. The YourNest team grows stronger with people who bring this kind of rigour and curiosity, and we're excited to see the impact she'll make. 

Welcome aboard, Saumya!

We are delighted to welcome Advait Mishra, who joins YourNest as our ESG Executive. In this role, he will conduct due diligence on environmental, social and governance-related parameters across our portfolio companies, helping ensure specific requirements and standards are met to mitigate non-financial risk, alongside regular reporting and tracking.

Advait brings experience across the cultural and heritage sectors, with brief stints in academic research and public relations. He studied History for his undergraduate degree at St. Stephen's College, and followed this up with a Master's in Modern South Asian Studies at the University of Cambridge. This academic foundation has shaped him to be meticulous in reading, writing and processing the material he handles. He describes looking at things in the “longue durée” as something that helps him contextualise better.

What sets Advait apart is a structured, multi-perspective approach to every problem he takes on, paired with a refusal to settle for a first draft. He sees his role as helping ensure that innovation across the portfolio is matched by the systems and practices needed for sustainable growth. The YourNest team grows stronger with people who bring this kind of rigour and curiosity, and we're excited to see the impact he'll make.

Welcome aboard, Advait!

Stephen King, the guru of strategic planning, once said advertising is both art and science. Our Venture Partner Mohit Hira – who spent many years in advertising – believes this is true of DeepTech investing too.

His essay, ‘The Art & Science of DeepTech Investing’, starts at a 1982 advertising congress and ends by detailing what it takes for a VC to back founders who are building at the bleeding edge of science and engineering. The science is the rigour: technology readiness, IP ownership, unit economics and governance. The art is spotting these ‘Challengineer’ founders before the evidence is obvious, and patiently staying with them through the long uneven road.

At YourNest, our dealflow team has looked at close to 30,000 pitches in the past 15 years; but we have invested in just 51. Mohit also explains why DeepTech needs patient capital, how 'Nurture Capital' works beyond the cheque, and what our exits – from Uniphore to the current portfolio – tell us about value creation.

Read the full article here: https://lnkd.in/gZQUW58T

𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗼𝗻𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗘𝗻𝗲𝗿𝗴𝘆 𝗧𝘂𝗿𝗻𝘀 𝟮𝟬𝟬 𝗜𝗖𝗘 𝗔𝘂𝘁𝗼𝘀 𝗘𝗹𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗰 𝗶𝗻 𝗕𝗲𝗻𝗴𝗮𝗹𝘂𝗿𝘂

Exponent Energy has completed 200 ICE-to-EV autorickshaw retrofits in Bengaluru through its Exponent OTO platform, demonstrating an alternative route to commercial vehicle electrification: converting vehicles already on the road instead of waiting for fleet replacement. 

𝗣𝗶𝗹𝗼𝘁 𝗦𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗨𝘁𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘀𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

• 200 autorickshaws retrofitted during a four-month pilot
• Fleet has covered 1.5+ million km
• More than 25,000 charging sessions completed
• Exponent claims around 20% share of Bengaluru’s electric 3W market 

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗧𝗲𝗰𝗵𝗻𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝘆

Exponent OTO combines the company’s battery, powertrain and vehicle software.

The retrofit can reportedly be completed in 24 hours, with a claimed 15-minute 0–100% charging time, 140–150 km real-world range and a five-year/3,000-cycle warranty. 

𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗥𝗲𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗳𝗶𝘁𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘀

India already has a massive installed base of ICE three-wheelers. Retrofitting could provide commercial drivers with a faster transition path while retaining the existing vehicle ecosystem.

Exponent is also using Exponent ONE to finance retrofit kits and reduce the upfront cost for drivers. The company plans to expand OTO to new electric three-wheelers through OEM partnerships as well. 

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗧𝗼 𝗪𝗮𝘁𝗰𝗵

The key test now is scale beyond the pilot — retrofit economics, regulatory approvals, financing, battery life and charging utilisation will determine whether this model can move from 200 vehicles to thousands across Indian cities.

𝗘𝗩 𝗕𝘂𝗹𝗹𝗲𝘁𝗶𝗻 𝗧𝗮𝗸𝗲

India’s commercial EV transition doesn’t necessarily require replacing every ICE vehicle.

If retrofit platforms can make existing autorickshaws economically viable as EVs, they could create a parallel pathway to electrification — particularly in high-utilisation urban 3W fleets.

Ayush Bhargava
